correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed: positive diagonal D_i and symmetric M_m imply chronology and reverse orders have equal trace and determinant; all permutations of ≤3 profiles are equivalent by dihedral symmetry; common four-step determinant is (1−2m)^4∏a_ib_i; Perron root is strictly increasing in trace at fixed determinant for strictly positive 2×2 matrices; all three formal four-season trace-difference polynomials have been verified symbolically from the package checker and have strict signs for distinct sorted ratios; rank-one m=1/2 follows by direct multiplication. The exact rational example was rechecked using Fraction with independent determinant and characteristic-polynomial certificates. Finite experiments do not constitute the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is a complete strict ordering of all four-season permutations of four distinct positive patch-fitness profiles under symmetric dispersal, with a universal half-mixing reversal and a proof that cycles of length at most three cannot exhibit such an order effect. Targeted mathematical literature and research-record queries and full-text primary comparisons found work on temporal correlations, general seasonal dispersal, two-season periodic population dynamics, and separate spectral-radius mixing inequalities, but no theorem that implies this entire four-season statement. Historical priority is provisional and broader rearrangement literature is residual risk.
residual_risks: Broader abstract spectral rearrangement inequalities might imply this special four-factor result despite absence from targeted searches.
The published ecological text makes general temporal-autocorrelation claims, but no theorem-level full-corpus dominance proof was possible; historical priority remains provisional.
The strictly ordered ratios and fixed symmetric dispersal are material scope restrictions; extension to arbitrary patch networks is not claimed.

value.rationale: There is a natural fixed-resource temporal planning decision: how to order four predetermined environmental seasons for a population moving between two patches. The four-season cycle is proved minimal for any order effect; three strictly ranked temporal classes exhaust the 24 calendars; the 50% migration sign reversal distinguishes habitat memory from nearly obligatory switching; a fully rational example shows the change in calendar can cross the linear invasion growth threshold. This is a structural classification with a motivated ecological outcome, not a renaming, numerical recomputation or arbitrary table. Limits are fixed two-patch symmetric mixing and linear invasion growth.
